thread:
Priya: Quick idea for packaging that might cut through a lot of back-and-forth: introduce QoS bands (gold/silver/bronze) + a small pool of 'grace tokens' per customer for burst. Also expose a Quota Elevation API so apps can request temporary uplifts instead of buying large commits. Thoughts?

Ethan: Interesting. QoS bands map to latency/throughput guarantees? gold = <150ms tail, silver = <300ms, bronze = best-effort? How to price?

Priya: Yes. Each band has a baseline SLA and a billing multiplier. Grace tokens are free monthly bursts (e.g., 5M tokens) to smooth spikes; Quota Elevation is an API that grants short-lived boosts (minutes-hours) billed at a premium.

Lina: Sales + CSM note: customers like predictability. The Elevation API could be a good sell for teams that hate long contract cycles. But we need clear guardrails to avoid abuse. Rate-limit elevations and require a billing token.

Diego: Runtime concerns: we need a way to tag requests with band metadata and honor band priority in scheduler. Also grace tokens must be accounted atomically to avoid double-spend across replicas.

Hannah: Finance: multipliers are doable. Suggest a modeling approach: base per-token cost by band (bronze = 1.0, silver = 1.25, gold = 1.7). Elevations billed at 2.5x real-time rate. Grace tokens are amortized into base price but tracked on ledger.

Ethan: Implementation sketch:
- product config: bands + grace_pool + elevation_policy
- runtime: request tag -> band -> scheduler priority
- billing: ledger for grace & elevation charges
Example config snippet:
```yaml
bands:
  gold:
    tail_latency_ms: 150
    base_multiplier: 1.7
  silver:
    tail_latency_ms: 300
    base_multiplier: 1.25
  bronze:
    tail_latency_ms: 1000
    base_multiplier: 1.0
grace:
  monthly_tokens: 5000000
  rollover: false
elevation:
  max_duration_minutes: 180
  max_concurrent_elevations: 2
```

Priya: Nice. Need to define UX: Console mapping (route -> default band), SDK helper to request elevation with callback URL, and an admin path to approve billing exceptions for pilots.

Lina: For pilots, offer a small amount of reserved gold for 90 days at a steep discount + elevated support. That should win over product-led trials that need predictable UX.

Diego: On the safety side: if we overcommit gold reservations and capacity is constrained, what is the degradation plan? We should support graceful demotion: temporarily move some gold traffic to silver with a customer-visible event and credits if SLA missed.

Hannah: Credit model: SLA breaches credit X% of monthly band fees proportional to unmet latency SLOs. For grace/elevation we can cap credits to avoid outsized liability. Legal will want caps.

Ethan: Engineering estimate: core routing + scheduler changes = 3 sprints (2 engs). Billing ledger & elevation API = 2 sprints (1 eng). Console + SDK + docs = 2 sprints (1 eng, 1 PM). Total ~7 engineer-sprints over 5-6 calendar weeks with overlap.

Priya: Proposed launch criteria:
1) runtime honors bands and exposes per-band metrics
2) billing ledger for grace tokens & elevation working end-to-end
3) Console route-band mapping & SDK elevation flow
4) pilot with at least 2 customers (one PLG, one enterprise)
5) legal pilot addendum + SLA language drafted
6) runbook for demotion & crediting in ops

Lina: I'd add migration criteria: existing commit customers mapped to an equivalent band allocation plus a one-time grace token top-up. That reduces churn.

Diego: Ops note: need telemetry flags to surface grace token exhaustion and elevation events in Console. Also include a safety throttle that denies elevations during infra incidents.

finance-bot: FYI: preliminary model suggests gold reserved discounts should be >30% vs pay-as-you-go to justify commits. Will upload spreadsheet.

Hannah: Legal ask: define the credit calculation formula and an official cap on SLA credits per period. I'll draft terms and share.

Priya: Ok next steps: I'll write an RFC with the config schema + SLA sketches. Ethan can add the scheduler design. Lina will outline pilot offers; Hannah + finance will finalize pricing ranges. Diego please list runtime caveats.

Ethan: I'll add a short perf test plan for gold vs silver vs bronze in the RFC.

Lina: I'll start talking to two pilot candidates (Maple & Orion).

Diego: Noted. I'll prototype grace token ledger behavior and post results.

ops-bot: Reminder: telemetry maintenance window tomorrow 03:00-04:00 UTC may delay some metric ingestion.

Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll circulate RFC by EOD tomorrow and tag reviewers.

Hannah: Ping me once RFC is up; I'll slot legal review.

finance-bot: I'll attach the pricing sensitivity model to the RFC.
